task.description:
This run (WF03-ISS0438-20260904) resolves ISS-0438 -- a scoping/architecture decision on whether Letflow ports R-Co's dynamic entity/data-model subsystem. The outcome is 'IN SCOPE, port now, as new S6 requirements' (CODE-DESIGNER's recommendation, CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASSed, REQ-VALIDATOR PASSed 7 resulting requirements REQ-225..231 after one rework iteration). No docs/migration/decisions/ record was written, because the decision-record path was only the OUT-OF-SCOPE branch's requirement (AC3) -- this run took the IN-SCOPE branch instead, whose evidence trail is the CODE-DESIGNER artefact plus the 7 gated requirements. Your job, per your normal REVIEWER duties (decision-record consistency, scope creep, idiom -- ORCHESTRATOR.md), is to independently gate the FINAL STATE of this run before Step Final merges it:

1. Read lib/letflow/design/iss0438-entity-subsystem-scoping.md in full -- confirm the recommendation is genuinely reasoned (not a rubber-stamp) and does not silently contradict any existing docs/migration/decisions/ record. Check specifically against decision 0003 (schema-per-tenant conventions) and decision 0014 (scripting/plugin runtime strategy, since this subsystem's router row once carried an S5 hedge) for consistency.
2. Confirm lib/letflow/router.ex's 'Deferred routes' table was NOT edited by this run (it should not be -- the outcome was in-scope/port, not the out-of-scope/remove-rows path). Read the file and confirm both Entities/EntityQuery rows are unchanged.
3. Confirm docs/migration/stage-6-operational-cross-cutting.md's addendum (added by REQ-ANALYST) is genuinely additive -- the pre-existing 'S6 is now complete' line and the 2026-09-01 REQ-211/212 addendum must both still read exactly as before, byte for byte, with only a new paragraph appended after them.
4. Spot-check at least two of the seven new requirements (REQ-225..231) in docs/requirements.yaml directly for idiomatic fit with this project's existing conventions -- tenant-scoping via prefix/tenant_id, no premature route/controller work, correct use of existing REQ-202/REQ-024 machinery rather than a parallel mechanism -- rather than trusting REQ-VALIDATOR's PASS alone (a second independent pass, per this project's redundancy principle).
5. Confirm no scope creep: this run produced ONLY a design artefact, 7 requirement entries, one stage-doc addendum paragraph, and (in a later step) a docs/issues/ISS-0438.yaml status update -- no lib/letflow/ implementation code, no migrations, matching ISS-0438's own AC7 ('no implementation of the subsystem is included in this issue').
6. State a PASS or FAIL verdict. This is a hard gate per your normal role -- do not rubber-stamp a producer's own claim of completeness.
acceptance_criteria: Design artefact independently checked against docs/migration/decisions/0003 and 0014 for consistency, not assumed consistent
router.ex's Deferred routes table confirmed byte-for-byte unchanged by this run
stage-6-operational-cross-cutting.md's addendum confirmed genuinely additive, pre-existing text unchanged
At least two of the seven new requirements independently spot-checked for idiomatic/architectural fit, not only trusted from REQ-VALIDATOR's PASS
No scope creep confirmed -- no lib/ or priv/repo/migrations/ files touched by this run
A clear PASS or FAIL verdict stated
